payload.scope: Count replayed payloads in the current matched frontend; never benchmark these probes.
caveats: Logical submitted payloads on every graph replay, not physical bus traffic or kernel direct reads.
Probe mutexes change execution: never infer lock counts or throughput from these binaries.

polling_build.scope: Isolate the current immutable completion observer's OS wakeup cost; polling is experimental.

timing: Clean DONE decode excludes loading,initialization,preparation and prefill;no internal timers or telemetry;unlocked clocks. Diagnostic durations are never performance evidence.
notes: User reported the machine idle before these repeats;background OS activity and unlocked clocks are not controlled.
Current frontend/math and matched cache margin1.5 from the earlier frozen build;input collections shared,not proof of final loaded ISA identity.
Separate call observer covers EXE imports and dynamically resolved entry points;vendor IAT hooks cover D3DKMT only. Private/inlined/driver locks and contention are not measured.
Payload probe counts logical runtime copies on every replay,not physical PCIe/VRAM traffic,kernel direct reads or staging memcpy. Its locks invalidate timing/lock comparisons.
Direct already submits cross-queue waits on the GPU;CPU completion waits publish host-visible results. CPU and GPU wait-call counts are not interchangeable work.
Full observer polling changes only immutable completion waiting on Windows;it consumes a CPU core while waiting and remains isolated.
The waiting ablation can also change CPU frequency and scheduling;its throughput change is not a pure OS-notification latency measurement.
Counts and policy fields identify remaining differences,not causation. Earlier rejected cache/SLM/GRF/indirect-length experiments retain their own profiles.
Archives preserve commands,source,logs,protocols and packet buffers. Binary/model packs have hashes;GGUF and weight-pack contents are not fully rehashed.
